P1.evidence: This is a second conversation and the rep opened by discarding everything from the first: 'It's been probably like 15 calls since I last spoke to you. So I don't want to operate under previous assumptions. So let's kind of treat this like a fresh call.' Honest, but the opposite of the intent behind P1a — the prospect had to restate his whole position. No frame of any kind was set; he went directly to 'Remind me, how can we potentially help you?' Agreement was a single 'Yeah' to the reset proposal.

P2.evidence: Scored rather than marked not applicable because the rep himself elected to run this as a fresh call. Age was asked ('Remind me, Cole, how old are you?'); height and current weight never were, and the only figure on record, 220 lb, is historical and volunteered. Work emerged obliquely through a goals question rather than a baseline one. No health-conditions question at all. Tight hips surfaced through the 1-10 scale and the rep did carry them forward ('you mentioned your hips') but never asked about them. Training week, diet, sleep and results were all volunteered or absent. On the positive side this is the one call in the batch where no medical condition existed to be missed.

P3.evidence: Excellent, and structured as a deliberate sweep. The 1-10 longevity scale ('ten is my body super prime for longevity, being able to do backflips when I'm 90') produced the mobility answer and the hips. Then 'What else are you, or who else, what else are you kind of doing this for?' produced the backpacking-with-my-daughter and grandfather-with-a-walker images. Then he worked each relationship in turn — 'you have a wife. Tell me how you want to show up for her by going to the next level for yourself' and 'how do you perceive being at a high level physically allowing you to pour at a high level into that?' — which reached the ministry and the faith identity. Only the explicit reflect-back was skipped.

P4.evidence: The root-cause question ran cleanly — 'You mentioned the streakiness, the inconsistency. What do you feel like was the origin of those things?' — and got a genuinely useful answer about how having a child changed which pockets of time he is willing to spend on himself. Then the same leading habit that recurs across this rep's calls: 'Would you say you've kind of been, you've gotten comfortable with that specifically?' supplied the label instead of letting him name it. P4f was never asked, though the prospect volunteered the answer himself and unusually well: 'as much as I try to do it on my own... maybe a little bit of pride in there, like, oh, I don't need help.'

P5.evidence: Complete in substance. Ran the comfort-zone frame and the skydiving question pre-emptively, got 'fear of failure', then the responsibility question — 'who's actually responsible, Cole, for taking that step?' / 'Me.' — then the readiness commit, 'So are you actually ready to take it?' / 'I am, yeah.' Then P5a directly: 'at the end of the day, my friend, what happens if you don't?' producing 'I won't ever succeed, so I will just stay where I'm at or get worse', and the settle check on top: 'You don't strike me as someone who's willing to take a step of that?' Only the explicit 'why not' was left unasked.

P6.evidence: P6a ran verbatim — 'do you feel internally capable, Cole, of following a step-by-step program and being a good student of Trevor to actually extract the value you want to extract?' — and got a yes. He also ran the counterfactual well ('if you had this program in your back pocket three years ago, where would you say you'd be today?'). P6b missed again, and this is now the fourth call in the batch where its absence let a spouse-plus-money blocker appear only after the price. The prospect's household rule about discussing anything over $100 is exactly the kind of thing 'is there any reason you wouldn't go all in' exists to surface, and it did not come out until the very end of the call.

P11.evidence: All three coaching tiers were declined and the $200/month option was deferred to a follow-up, so no payment, onboarding, agreement or welcome step was reachable.

objection_plays.detail: The most faithful run of this play in the batch. Isolated first — 'to put the investment aside for a second, Cole, do you want to do this?' — then reinforced with 'Why do you want to do this?', then the food-off-your-table framing, then the permission question near-verbatim: 'I just need to ask you a couple of questions financially... Do you mind me asking you a couple of questions on finances?' Then the financial picture: cash on hand (about $4-5K), how many credit cards (one), available credit (about the same), and credit score. NOT run: used versus available, crypto and investments, and the 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' frame. Most creditable part is what he did with the answer — he read the numbers and declined to take the money rather than pushing the card: 'the last thing I want for you to do is just take up your cash on hand, your credit card amount and just say, come in for the 9k, or even the 6.' He then partly undid that by inventing an unsanctioned $4,000 tier.

Triggered clearly and twice — 'I can't just pull that trigger by myself without talking to my wife' and later the household rule, 'we have a rule that we talk about things that are, like, over $100 purchase.' Not one OB move ran. He never asked her name, never asked whether she would be receptive, never asked whether it was permission or an FYI, never invited her onto the call, and never offered the deposit-and-refund fallback. He ran this play thoroughly on two other calls in the same batch, so it is a lapse rather than a capability gap — though with $4-5K liquid the deposit fallback would arguably have been the wrong thing to reach for.

Triggered — 'we just moved and stuff. So that sounds like it's going to be a bit much for me to handle right now.' None of the moves ran. The rep instead validated the timing objection outright: 'for people like yourself who really want to do the coaching... It's just not a good time, whether it's finances or whatever it is.' Defensible given what the financial picture had just revealed, but scored as a miss against the script.

Triggered on the downsell — 'I'll definitely think on it' and 'I think I just need to think about it just for a second.' One move ran, a reasonable version of the blocker question: 'Just so I'm on the same page as you, is there any reason why you don't want to, like, jump in with this, in this moment, or just help me understand?' It produced the household $100 rule. He then accepted it, booked a follow-up and stopped — no deciding-versus-thinking frame, no 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now', no confirmation question.

Run pre-emptively as a pre-close frame rather than in response to a stall, as on the John White call. The comfort-zone question, the skydiving setup ('they're on a plane, they're scared of heights, but they're about to go skydiving. What typically stops most people?'), the 'why do you say that' follow-up and the responsibility question all ran, and the prospect built the frame himself: 'it's a lot easier to just stay comfortable where you're at because it's familiar and easier.' Converted directly into the readiness commitment.

notes: Strongest phases 3 and 5 of the batch and by far the most honest money conversation — he opened the wallet properly, saw that the money was not there, and told the prospect not to spend it. That instinct is the right one and should be held up. Two things to coach: P6b, whose absence has now cost four calls in this batch by letting a spouse and a budget appear only after the price; and OB, which he runs well elsewhere and did not run here at all despite an explicit household veto rule. The $4,000 three-month tier should not exist.
